items.excerpt: The growing use of AI large language models could make human writing, perspectives and reasoning more alike, according to a research paper that raises questions about creative diversity and authorial voice.
Author Daisy Buchanan argues that handing routine writing tasks such as emails to ChatGPT quietly erodes the everyday craft skills writers depend on.
It's time for ideas to become solutions in the fight to protect authors' rights, writes Tom West, CEO of Publishers' Licensing Services, as AI licensing shifts from debate to an actual market.
In Love Machine (Faber & Faber), James Muldoon looks at real people's intimate relationships with AI chatbots, and how those bonds could change relationships among humans.
Tech developers think automation will fundamentally reshape the work of literary translators, but not everyone in publishing is on board.
A new app called iLands allows the creation of autonomous AI agents that not only write articles but pitch their work to media outlets.
GEO is generative engine optimization: trying to influence whether your name or book appears in AI overviews or in chatbot conversations, and it works differently from SEO.
Conference attendees have many questions about AI, and organizers would better serve their audience by engaging with intent and clarity instead of avoiding the topic.

The US DOJ filed a Statement of Interest in the copyright litigation between The New York Times and OpenAI/Microsoft, largely siding with the AI companies on LLM training as fair use. Publishing experts respond.
A new interactive exhibition about the writing of James Baldwin features an AI-programmed typewriter that directs users to writing drawn from Baldwin's books, essays, and letters.
Twelve years after Geek Sublime: The Beauty of Code, The Code of Beauty, Vikram Chandra revisits his ode to the craft of human coding in an era of vibe coding and generative AI.
The Flowtica Verso's always-on e-paper display sets it apart from standard screenless AI voice recorders, pairing capture and transcription with an E Ink reading surface.
Elsevier says its AI research platform LeapSpace now incorporates content from more than 1,500 scholarly publishers and societies, and has added an independent AI advisory board.
New infrastructure will make IOP content "licensed for inference, protected from training use, and fully tracked" when AI systems draw on it.
Clarivate's "Pulse of the Library" report found 28% of respondents in mainland China reported moderate to active AI implementation, ahead of other regions.
